name: Arr stack
summary: Request films and TV, and have them found, downloaded and filed into your Jellyfin or Plex library - all connected for you

options.label: Downloads and library folder
options.help: On a share. It gets torrents/ and usenet/ (downloads) and, unless you choose library folders below, media/ (the library: tv, movies, music, books) - point Jellyfin or Plex at media/. Library folders inside it get finished downloads linked into them (no copying, no double disk space): the recommended setup.

options.label: TV folders
options.help: Your own TV folders, anywhere on the NAS's shares (e.g. /mnt/HD/HD_a2/Me/TV) - the first is where new series go, and each is offered when adding one. Empty: media/tv in the folder above. Folders outside it get finished downloads copied into them, rather than linked; they must be writable by the share users' group.

options.label: Film folders
options.help: Your own film folders, anywhere on the NAS's shares (e.g. /mnt/HD/HD_a2/Me/Films) - the first is where new films go, and each is offered when adding one. Empty: media/movies in the folder above. Folders outside it get finished downloads copied into them, rather than linked; they must be writable by the share users' group.

options.label: Music folders
options.help: With Lidarr: your own music folders, anywhere on the NAS's shares (e.g. /mnt/HD/HD_a2/Me/Music) - the first is where new artists go. Empty: media/music in the folder above. Folders outside it get finished downloads copied into them, rather than linked; they must be writable by the share users' group.

options.label: Book folders
options.help: With Bookshelf: your own book folders, anywhere on the NAS's shares (e.g. /mnt/HD/HD_a2/Me/Books) - the first is where new authors go. Empty: media/books in the folder above. Folders outside it get finished downloads copied into them, rather than linked; they must be writable by the share users' group.

options.label: After a download is filed
options.help: Keep seeding: torrents stay in qBittorrent (the library's copy is a link to the same data - or a copy, in folders outside the downloads folder). Seed for a while: qBittorrent stops each at the ratio or number of days below, then it's removed with its files - only the library's copy is left. Don't seed: removed as soon as it's filed (some trackers expect seeding). Usenet downloads are always removed once filed.

choices.label: Seed for a while, then remove

options.label: Seed until the ratio
options.help: With "Seed for a while": uploaded / downloaded. Whichever comes first, this or the days below.

options.label: Seed for up to (days)
options.help: With "Seed for a while": 0 for no time limit.

options.label: Rename what's filed
options.help: Tidy names (e.g. Show - S01E02 - Title), as Jellyfin and Plex like them, using each app's naming settings. Off: names kept as downloaded.

options.label: Films without their own folder
options.help: Radarr keeps each film in a folder of its own (Films/Name (2024)/Name (2024).mkv). On: once filed, each film's files are moved up into the film folder (Films/Name (2024).mkv) and the film is taken off Radarr's list - so Radarr won't upgrade or rename it, but won't fetch it again either. Seerr then sees it through Jellyfin or Plex. A film whose name is already there keeps its folder.

options.label: Media server
options.help: The one on this NAS (or your network) showing the library: Sonarr, Radarr and Lidarr tell it about each new file, so it appears straight away rather than at its next scan. Seerr asks for it once, on its own setup page.

options.label: Media server's key
options.help: Jellyfin or Emby: an API key - made on its dashboard (Dashboard -> API Keys -> +). Plex: its token - left empty, it's read from Plex on this NAS (its Preferences.xml); for another Plex, see Plex's support article "Finding an authentication token".

options.label: Media server's address
options.help: Empty: on this NAS, at its usual port (Plex http://host.docker.internal:32400, Jellyfin and Emby http://host.docker.internal:8096 - host.docker.internal being the NAS, as the apps see it). Elsewhere: e.g. http://192.168.1.20:8096.

options.label: ntfy topic
options.help: With the ntfy app on this NAS: notifications to this topic - subscribe to it in the ntfy app on your phone. Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr and Bookshelf: something filed, upgraded or failed, or needing you; Prowlarr: health problems; Seerr: new requests, available, failed, issues. Connected with the ntfy app's own token. Empty: no notifications.

options.label: Quality rules (Recyclarr)
options.help: Which download is "best": the TRaSH Guides' tested profiles for Sonarr and Radarr - preferring good release groups and sources, avoiding poor encodes, fakes and re-encodes - kept up to date daily by Recyclarr. Seerr uses them for requests; series and films already added keep their profile (change it in Sonarr or Radarr). About 50MB of memory.

options.label: Quality for requests
options.help: With the quality rules, both are made in Sonarr and Radarr: 1080p (WEB-1080p, HD Bluray + WEB) and 4K (WEB-2160p, UHD Bluray + WEB: 4K only, several times the disk space). This is the one Seerr's requests use - either can be picked for each series or film in Sonarr or Radarr.

options.label: User name
options.help: For every app's web interface (qBittorrent, Prowlarr, Sonarr, Radarr, Bazarr...). Seerr has its own users: those of your Jellyfin or Plex.

options.label: Password
options.help: For every app's web interface, with the user name above. Changing it here changes it in every app.

options.label: Music (Lidarr)
options.help: Albums by the artists you follow, filed into media/music (for Navidrome, Jellyfin or Plex). About 250MB of memory.

options.label: Books (Bookshelf)
options.help: E-books and audiobooks by the authors you follow, filed into media/books (for Calibre-Web or Audiobookshelf). Bookshelf continues Readarr, with Hardcover's book data. About 250MB of memory.

options.label: Usenet downloads (SABnzbd)
options.help: Downloads from Usenet as well as torrents - it needs a Usenet provider's account (added in SABnzbd afterwards). About 150MB of memory.

options.label: FlareSolverr
options.help: Gets Prowlarr past Cloudflare's "checking your browser" page, which some indexers have: tag those indexers flaresolverr in Prowlarr. It runs a browser: about 500MB of memory.

options.label: Subtitle language
options.help: What Bazarr looks for. More languages, and subtitle sources with accounts, can be added in Bazarr.

options.label: Torrent port
options.help: qBittorrent's incoming connections. Forwarding it on your router (TCP and UDP) helps downloads, but isn't needed.
